_comment: GRAND over the FULL Lima DEM (10886 x 9638 px, ~105 Mpx). The third department run, and a deliberate repeat of grand_arequipa_full.json and grand_ancash_full.json: every physics and layout criterion is copied from them unchanged, so a difference in the answer is a difference in the terrain. Lima is the coastal contrast -- desert shelf, the western Andean flank, and the Cordillera Huayhuash in its north-east corner -- against Arequipa's high plateau and Ancash's Cordillera Blanca. SRTMGL1 like the other two, deliberately: the older lima_AW3D30.tif would have put a dataset difference inside every comparison.
_comment_downsample: 4, matching the Arequipa and Ancash pairs so all three are comparable. Lima is 105 Mpx, between Ancash's 69 and Arequipa's 129. Estimated 4.22 GiB for the search plus 0.42 for the map at ds 4 / stride 5, against ~7.4 GiB available. Read the areas as lower bounds for the usual two reasons: area is measured on the downsampled mask while capacity is measured at full resolution, and striding fragments the mask -- which costs TAMBO far more than the 4.75x of ROADMAP 6.34, measured at 291x on the Huaylas crop (ROADMAP 6.49). The ratios between regions survive both biases because all three runs carry them equally; the absolute TAMBO numbers do not.
_comment_rfi: none, as for Ancash and for the same reason. There IS a 'lima' RFI preset, but using it here would make Lima the only one of the three department runs with settlement exclusion of its own kind -- Arequipa uses its preset, Ancash uses none. Holding it at none keeps Lima comparable to Ancash, and the difference against Arequipa is stated there: its five circles cover ~3,500 km2 of a ~120,000 km2 box, so roughly 2.9%.
_comment_origin: Deliberately null: read from the DEM's own ModelTiepointTag. The crop configs carry the crop's corner, which is not this file's.
